newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech Skoda Praha plans new n-plant bid.
newsitem.headline: Czech Skoda Praha plans new n-plant bid.

text.p: Czech engineering firm Skoda Praha a.s. will enter a tender to complete two blocks at Slovakia's Mochovce nuclear power plant, with an estimated 36 billion Slovak crown bid, a company official said on Wednesday.

Spokesman Milan Kuchta told Reuters that the firm would submit its bid to become the general technology supplies contractor for the plant's third and fourth blocks, which should be completed around the year 2003.

Skoda, no longer affiliated with the Plzen-based concern of the same name, or with the car maker Skoda Auto a.s., won the contract to lead the completion of the first two blocks of the same power station, operated by state utility Slovenske Elektrarne a.s..
"The third and fourth blocks should be equipped with the same reactors as the first two, that means (Russian-designed) VVER 440," Kuchta said.
He added that the first two blocks, at which Skoda cooperates with Germany's Siemens AG and France's Framatome, should be opened in 1998 and 1999.
The other two are now 25 percent complete.
The plant has been widely criticised by environmentalists as outdated, dangerous and unreliable.
Work on the plant at Mochovce began in mid-1980s, but was suspended in 1989 after the project ran into financial problems and required safety upgrades.

The government signed a $900 million financing package in May with Czech, French, German and Slovak banks, allowing continuation in the project, and an additional $150 million deal with Russia which included upgrading of construction documentation and fuel future supplies.

The safety of the Russian designed VVER 440/213 reactors is based on recommendations of the Vienna-based International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) and Risc Audit evaluation, the joint organisations of German and French nuclear safety bodies.
